subject: BlueHarbor: continuity cutover request — westus2 throughput collapse
messages:
From: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@blueharbormedia.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: support@blueharbormedia.com
Date: 10 Sep 2028 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Production spike — westus2 throughput collapse (urgent)

Logan,

We started seeing a dramatic drop in processed requests for our production shard in us-west-2 around 07:50 UTC — throughput collapsed by ~85% and clients are seeing sustained 5xxs. Automatic routing pushed traffic to us-east-1 but the application latency ballooned and our customers are calling in. Attached is a short log sample with consecutive 502/503s and the initial trace.

Can Redwood execute a continuity cutover or any immediate mitigation? This is P0 for BlueHarbor — their payment flows are impacted. We need executive visibility and an ETA on when traffic will be stable.

Attachments: blueharbor-prod-5xx-sample.log (text)

—Emma
Senior Ops, BlueHarbor Media
emma.lewis@blueharbormedia.com
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@blueharbormedia.com>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: 10 Sep 2028 08:25:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production spike — westus2 throughput collapse (urgent)

Thanks Emma — sorry for the disruption, we see the same alerting pattern on our side. I'm escalating to SRE and routing leads now and will coordinate a continuity cutover. High-level plan:

- Immediate: gather health/queue diagnostics from westus2 (rishi + markus)
- Near-term: canary steer a fraction of new sessions to us-east-1 while we confirm backend health
- If metrics stabilize: ramp steering to complete swap and drain westus2

I've opened JIRA SUP-2459 and attached a diagnostic packet for our internal use. Hannah, Rishi — can you validate the canary thresholds and whether we can do a site-swap with a 5% -> 50% ramp? Marissa, looping you for customer comms and exec note.

Attachment: diagnostic_packet_20280910.tar.gz (support bundle)

—Logan
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 10 Sep 2028 08:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production spike — westus2 throughput collapse (urgent)

Quick diagnostic from the westus2 fleet (live sampling):
- Observed sudden queue-depth growth on inference-gpu-pool-7 starting 07:48 UTC
- CPU on the control-plane proxy nodes climbed to 96% and request latency spiked before 5xxs surfaced
- No obvious network partition to the datastore; KV cache hit-rate unchanged

Immediate recommendation: start a conservative canary (5% new sessions to us-east-1) while we stream flow traces. If canary shows error-rate drop and tail latency < 300ms we can accelerate to 50% and then drain.

I'm attaching a short flow trace and a sample of the failing request IDs. I'll shepherd the canary while Rishi prepares the drain commands.

Attachment: flow-trace-westus2.txt (text)

Hannah
Head of Routing Operations — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 10 Sep 2028 08:52:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production spike — proposed canary and thresholds

Agreed with Hannah's approach. Concrete action plan and rollback:
1) Execute canary: route 5% of new sessions to us-east-1 (start 08:55 UTC)
2) Monitor for 10 minutes. Success criteria to continue ramp:
   - 5xx rate in canary <= baseline + 2% absolute
   - P95 latency in canary < 300ms
3) Ramp to 50% over next 8 minutes if success criteria met
4) If 5xx rises above baseline + 5% or P95 > 500ms during ramp -> immediate rollback to original routing

I'll also run a pre-drain check on the westus2 GPU nodes (mem/cold-start queues). Markus — I need the drain playbook commands and whether there's any stateful session affinity to consider.

Note: canary and ramp will temporarily exceed our documented SLA window; request approval for a minor SLA exception for this continuity action.

—Rishi
SRE Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 10 Sep 2028 09:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production spike — customer communication

Approved. Please proceed with the canary and keep me posted every 10 minutes; I'll prepare the customer-facing summary and escalation note for BlueHarbor execs. Draft blurb for Emma: 

"We are performing a controlled continuity cutover to an alternate region to stabilize traffic. We will provide progress updates at 10-minute intervals and confirm when normal processing resumes."

If the canary looks good, we should proactively offer a 10% credit for today's disruption (pre-approved by revenue ops last quarter for P0 continuity events).

—Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lewis <emma.lewis@blueharbormedia.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: 10 Sep 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production spike — completion of cutover and initial metrics

Emma — update and actions taken: 

- At 08:55 UTC we initiated a 5% canary to us-east-1. Observed immediate drop in 5xxs to baseline within 3 mins.
- At 09:03 UTC we ramped to 50% and then 100% by 09:09 UTC; westus2 is now in drain mode.
- Post-shift metrics attached; 5xx rate is down to expected baseline and P95 latency for BlueHarbor requests is ~210ms in us-east-1.

Attachments: post-shift-metrics-20280910.csv (metrics snapshot)

Next steps: leave westus2 draining for 2 hours, collect heap/core dumps if any new failures surface, and run a root-cause follow-up postmortem. Marissa will send the customer exec note and credit details.

Sorry again for the impact — we prioritized continuity and kept customer traffic moving. I'll keep this thread active for the postmortem.

—Logan
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
